modules.title: The age of the universe
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Integrating `dt = da / (a H)` from `a = 0` to the present value of the scale factor, with
`H = H₀ E(a / a₀)` for a reduced Hubble function `E` (for instance `reducedHubble` of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.ReducedHubble`), gives the age of the universe
`t₀ = H₀⁻¹ ∫₀¹ dx / (x E(x))`. It is proportional to `1 / H₀`: the dimensionless integral depends
only on the shape of `E`.

The age is defined here for an arbitrary function `E`, as an interval integral; no convergence
is asserted.

## ii. Key results

- `age`: `t₀ = H₀⁻¹ ∫₀¹ dx / (x E(x))`.
- `age_eq`: `t₀ ∝ 1 / H₀`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The age of the universe

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric
modules.doc:
The spatial geometry of an FLRW model and its curvature parameter, the structures `FLRW` and
`CosmicFluid`, the density and pressure of the cosmological constant as a fluid and the cosmic
fluid with the cosmological constant folded in, the tangent-line bound for an FLRW model whose
scale factor decelerates and the resulting lower bound on its interval of time, the first- and
second-order Friedmann equations, the proposition `FLRW.FriedmannSolution` that a model and a
fluid solve them, and the Hubble and deceleration parameters.

declarations.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry
declarations.doc:
The inductive type with three constructors:
- `Spherical (k : ℝ)`
- `Flat`
- `Saddle (k : ℝ)`
declarations.statement:
inductive SpatialGeometry : Type where
  | Spherical (k : ℝ) (h : k < 0)
  | Flat
  | Saddle (k : ℝ) (h : k > 0)

declarations.doc:
For `s` corresponding to
- `Spherical k`, `S s r = k * sin (r / k)`
- `Flat`, `S s r = r`,
- `Saddle k`, `S s r = k * sinh (r / k)`.

declarations.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.mul_sinh_as_div
declarations.doc:

First show that `k * sinh(r / k) = sinh(r / k) / (1 / k)` pointwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_sinh_as_div (r k : ℝ) :
    k * Real.sinh (r / k) = Real.sinh (r / k) / (1 / k)

declarations.name: Cosmology.SpatialGeometry.curvature
declarations.doc:
The curvature parameter of the spatial geometry, the constant `k` of the first-order
  Friedmann equation `FLRW.FriedmannEquation.FirstOrderFriedmann`:
- `1 / k ^ 2` for `Spherical k`, whose profile `S` is that of a sphere of radius `|k|`,
- `0` for `Flat`,
- `-1 / k ^ 2` for `Saddle k`, whose profile `S` is that of a hyperbolic space of curvature

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW
declarations.doc:
An FLRW model: the scale factor `a` of the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric on an
open interval `I` of cosmic time, positive and twice differentiable on `I`, together with the
geometry of the spatial slices. The values of `a` outside `I` carry no meaning. The interval
lets a model begin at a Big Bang, as the Milne model `FLRW.milne` does on
`I = {t | 0 < t.val}`.
declarations.statement:
structure FLRW where
  /-- The interval of cosmic time on which the model is defined. -/
  I : Set Time
  /-- The interval `I` is open. -/
  isOpen_I : IsOpen I
  /-- The set `I` is an interval. -/
  ordConnected_I : I.OrdConnected
  /-- The scale factor as a function of cosmic time. -/
  a : Time → ℝ
  /-- The scale factor is positive on `I`. -/
  a_pos : ∀ t ∈ I, 0 < a t
  /-- The scale factor is differentiable on `I`. -/
  differentiableOn_a : DifferentiableOn ℝ a I
  /-- The time derivative of the scale factor is differentiable on `I`. -/
  differentiableOn_deriv_a : DifferentiableOn ℝ (∂ₜ a) I
  /-- The geometry of the spatial slices. -/
  geometry : SpatialGeometry

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.scaleFactor_le_tangent
declarations.doc:
If the scale factor decelerates on the interval (`∂ₜ ∂ₜ a ≤ 0` on `U.I`), it lies below its
tangent line at any time `t₀` of `U.I`: `a t ≤ a t₀ + ∂ₜ a t₀ (t - t₀)` for `t ∈ U.I`. The
derivative is antitone on the segment between `t` and `t₀`, which lies in `U.I`, and the mean
value inequality concludes.
declarations.statement:
lemma scaleFactor_le_tangent (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0) {t₀ t : Time}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (ht : t ∈ U.I) : U.a t ≤ U.a t₀ + ∂ₜ U.a t₀ * (t.val - t₀.val)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lt_of_mem_I_of_decelerating
declarations.doc:
The Big-Bang bound for an FLRW model: if the scale factor decelerates on `U.I` and the model
expands at `t₀ ∈ U.I`, every time of `U.I` is later than `t₀ - a t₀ / ∂ₜ a t₀`. Earlier, the
tangent line, and hence the scale factor, would be non-positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma lt_of_mem_I_of_decelerating (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0)
    {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    t₀.val - U.a t₀ / ∂ₜ U.a t₀ < t.val

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.bddBelow_I_of_decelerating
declarations.doc:
Hence the interval of an FLRW model that decelerates on `U.I` and expands at one of its
times is bounded below.
declarations.statement:
lemma bddBelow_I_of_decelerating (U : FLRW) (hdec : ∀ s ∈ U.I, ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) s ≤ 0) {t₀ : Time}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) : BddBelow U.I

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.FirstOrderFriedmann
declarations.doc:
The first-order Friedmann equation.

- `a : Time → ℝ` is the FLRW scale factor as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `ρ : Time → ℝ` is the total energy density as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `k : ℝ` is the spatial curvature parameter.
- `Λ : ℝ` is the cosmological constant.
- `G : ℝ` is Newton's constant.
- `c : SpeedOfLight` is the speed of light; take `c = 1` for units in which it is one.

Note: We will leave `c` explicit for generality and accounting purposes.

At time `t` the equation reads:
`(a'(t) / a(t))^2 = (8πG/3) ρ(t) − k c^2 / a(t)^2 + Λ c^2 / 3`.
declarations.statement: def FirstOrderFriedmann (a ρ : Time → ℝ) (k Λ G : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : Prop

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.SecondOrderFriedmann
declarations.doc:
The second-order Friedmann equation.
Note: Other sources may call this the Raychaudhuri equation.
We choose not to use that terminology to avoid the Raychaudhuri equation
related to describing congruences of geodesics in general relativity.
- `a : Time → ℝ` is the FLRW scale factor as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `ρ : Time → ℝ` is the total energy density as a function of cosmic time `t`.
- `p : Time → ℝ` is the pressure. It is related to `ρ` via `p = w * ρ `
- `w` is the equation of state. We will introduce this later.
- `Λ : ℝ` is the cosmological constant.
- `G : ℝ` is Newton's constant.
- `c : SpeedOfLight` is the speed of light; take `c = 1` for units in which it is one.

Note: We will leave `c` explicit for generality and accounting purposes.

At time `t` the equation reads:
`(a''(t) / a (t)) = - (4πG/3) * (ρ(t) + 3 * p(t) / c^2) + Λ * c^2 / 3`.
declarations.statement: def SecondOrderFriedmann (a ρ p : Time → ℝ) (Λ G : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : Prop

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_hubbleConstant
declarations.doc:
Quotient-rule expression for the time derivative of the Hubble constant:
`dₜ H = (a'' a - (a')^2) / a^2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_hubbleConstant {a : Time → ℝ} {t : Time}
    (ha : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd_a : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (haz : a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (hubbleConstant a) t =
      (∂ₜ (∂ₜ a) t * a t - (∂ₜ a t) ^ 2) / (a t) ^ 2

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.decelerationParameter_eq_one_plus_hubbleConstant
declarations.doc: The deceleration parameter is equal to `- (1 + (dₜ H)/H^2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma decelerationParameter_eq_one_plus_hubbleConstant
    {a : Time → ℝ} {t : Time}
    (ha : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd_a : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (haz : a t ≠ 0) (hd_az : ∂ₜ a t ≠ 0) :
    decelerationParameter a t =
      -(1 + ∂ₜ (hubbleConstant a) t / (hubbleConstant a t) ^ 2)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_hubbleConstant_eq_neg_sq_mul
declarations.doc: The time derivative of the Hubble constant equals `-H² (1 + q)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_hubbleConstant_eq_neg_sq_mul
    {a : Time → ℝ} {t : Time}
    (ha : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd_a : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (haz : a t ≠ 0) (hd_az : ∂ₜ a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (hubbleConstant a) t =
      -(hubbleConstant a t) ^ 2 * (1 + decelerationParameter a t)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_hubbleConstant_neg_iff
declarations.doc:
Pointwise: `∂ₜ H t < 0` iff `-1 < q t` (assuming `a` is twice differentiable at `t`
and both `a t` and `∂ₜ a t` are nonzero).
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_hubbleConstant_neg_iff
    {a : Time → ℝ} {t : Time}
    (ha : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd_a : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (haz : a t ≠ 0) (hd_az : ∂ₜ a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (hubbleConstant a) t < 0 ↔ -1 < decelerationParameter a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.exists_deriv_hubbleConstant_neg_iff
declarations.doc:
There exists a time at which `∂ₜ H < 0` iff there exists a time with `q > -1`.

(The corresponding informal statement was written with `q < -1`. Since
`dₜ H = -H² (1 + q)` and `H ≠ 0`, one has `dₜ H < 0 ↔ q > -1`, so the formal
statement uses the corrected inequality `-1 < q`.)
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_deriv_hubbleConstant_neg_iff
    {a : Time → ℝ}
    (ha : ∀ t, DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd_a : ∀ t, DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (haz : ∀ t, a t ≠ 0) (hd_az : ∀ t, ∂ₜ a t ≠ 0) :
    (∃ t, ∂ₜ (hubbleConstant a) t < 0) ↔ (∃ t, -1 < decelerationParameter a t)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution
declarations.doc:
The proposition that the FLRW model `U` filled with the cosmic fluid `F` solves the
Friedmann equations: the first- and second-order Friedmann equations, with cosmological
constant `Λ`, Newton's constant `G` and speed of light `c`, hold at every time of the interval
`U.I`, the curvature parameter being the one of the spatial geometry. The continuity equation
of the fluid is not part of it: it follows from the two Friedmann equations
(`FLRW.FriedmannSolution.continuityEquation` in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.MatterContent`).
declarations.statement:
structure FriedmannSolution (U : FLRW) (F : CosmicFluid) (Λ G : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) : Prop where
  /-- The first-order Friedmann equation holds on `U.I`. -/
  firstOrder : ∀ t ∈ U.I, FirstOrderFriedmann U.a F.ρ U.geometry.curvature Λ G c t
  /-- The second-order Friedmann equation holds on `U.I`. -/
  secondOrder : ∀ t ∈ U.I, SecondOrderFriedmann U.a F.ρ F.p Λ G c t

modules.title: Density parameters and the closure relation
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The first-order Friedmann equation of `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`,
`H² = (8 π G / 3) ρ - k c² / a² + Λ c² / 3`, can be read as a budget for the expansion rate `H`.

The critical density `ρ_cr = 3 H² / (8 π G)` is the density for which this equation holds with
`k = 0` and `Λ = 0`. When `Λ = 0`, a universe denser than `ρ_cr` is spatially closed (`k > 0`), a
less dense one is open (`k < 0`), and one at exactly `ρ_cr` is flat.

Measuring each term in units of `ρ_cr` gives the density parameter `Ω = ρ / ρ_cr` of a fluid, the
density parameter `Ω_Λ = Λ c² / (3 H²)` of the cosmological constant and the curvature density
parameter `Ω_K = - k c² / (H² a²)`. Dividing the Friedmann equation by `H²` gives the closure
relation `Ω + Ω_Λ + Ω_K = 1`.

These quantities are defined for an FLRW model. For a solution of the Friedmann equations, the
closure relation holds at every time of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`.

The reduced Hubble function of the standard cosmological model is in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.ReducedHubble`, and the age of the universe in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Age`.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.criticalDensity`, `FLRW.densityParameter`, `FLRW.curvatureDensityParameter`,
  `FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter`: the critical density and the density parameters of an FLRW
  model.
- `FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter_eq_densityParameter`,
  `FLRW.densityParameter_addCosmologicalConstant`: `Ω_Λ` is the density parameter of the
  cosmological constant as a fluid.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_lambda_add_curvature`,
  `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_curvature`: the closure relations
  `Ω + Ω_Λ + Ω_K = 1` and, for `Λ = 0`, `Ω + Ω_K = 1`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The critical density and the density parameters
- B. The closure relation

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.criticalDensity
declarations.doc:
The critical density `ρ_cr = 3 H² / (8 π G)` of an FLRW model at time `t`, where `H` is the
Hubble parameter of its scale factor. It is the density of a spatially flat universe without
cosmological constant expanding at the rate `H`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def criticalDensity (G : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.densityParameter
declarations.doc: The density parameter `Ω = ρ / ρ_cr` of a cosmic fluid in an FLRW model.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def densityParameter (F : CosmicFluid) (G : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.curvatureDensityParameter
declarations.doc:
The curvature density parameter `Ω_K = - k c² / (H² a²)` of an FLRW model, where `k` is the
curvature parameter of its spatial geometry. When `H` and `a` are nonzero, it is positive for a
saddle geometry, negative for a spherical one and zero for the flat one.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def curvatureDensityParameter (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter
declarations.doc:
The density parameter `Ω_Λ = Λ c² / (3 H²)` of the cosmological constant in an FLRW
model.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lambdaDensityParameter (Λ : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.lambdaDensityParameter_eq_densityParameter
declarations.doc:
For `G ≠ 0`, `Ω_Λ` is the density parameter of the empty fluid with the cosmological constant
folded in.
declarations.statement:
lemma lambdaDensityParameter_eq_densityParameter {Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hG : G ≠ 0)
    (t : Time) :
    U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t
      = U.densityParameter (CosmicFluid.empty.addCosmologicalConstant Λ G c) G t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.densityParameter_addCosmologicalConstant
declarations.doc:
For `G ≠ 0`, folding the cosmological constant into a cosmic fluid adds `Ω_Λ` to its
density parameter.
declarations.statement:
lemma densityParameter_addCosmologicalConstant (F : CosmicFluid) {Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (hG : G ≠ 0) (t : Time) :
    U.densityParameter (F.addCosmologicalConstant Λ G c) G t
      = U.densityParameter F G t + U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_lambda_add_curvature
declarations.doc:
The closure relation `Ω + Ω_Λ + Ω_K = 1` for a solution of the Friedmann equations, at the
times of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma densityParameter_add_lambda_add_curvature (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c) {t : Time}
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    U.densityParameter F G t + U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t
      + U.curvatureDensityParameter c t = 1

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.densityParameter_add_curvature
declarations.doc:
The closure relation `Ω + Ω_K = 1` for a solution of the Friedmann equations without
cosmological constant, at the times of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma densityParameter_add_curvature (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I)

    U.densityParameter F G t + U.curvatureDensityParameter c t = 1

modules.title: The de Sitter solution of the Friedmann equations
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The de Sitter solution of the Friedmann equations (`FirstOrderFriedmann` and
`SecondOrderFriedmann` of `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`): the scale factor
`a(t) = a₀ exp(σ √(Λ/3) c t)`, `σ = ±1`, solves both equations with `ρ = 0`, `p = 0`, flat
spatial slices and `Λ > 0`; its Hubble parameter is constant and its deceleration parameter is
`q = -1`. As an FLRW model filled with the empty cosmic fluid, `FLRW.deSitter`, it is defined at
all times: its interval of time is not bounded below, whereas a solution with `0 ≤ ρ`, `0 ≤ p`
and `Λ = 0` that expands at one time has a Big Bang
(`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution`).

## ii. Key results

- `deSitterScaleFactor`: `a(t) = a₀ exp(σ √(Λ/3) c t)` with `σ = ±1`.
- `deSitterScaleFactor_firstOrderFriedmann`, `deSitterScaleFactor_secondOrderFriedmann`:
  it solves both Friedmann equations with `ρ = 0`, `p = 0`, `k = 0` and `Λ > 0`.
- `hubbleConstant_deSitterScaleFactor`: its Hubble parameter is the constant `σ √(Λ/3) c`
  (for any `σ`, `Λ`, `c`).
- `decelerationParameter_deSitterScaleFactor`: its deceleration parameter is `q = -1`.
- `FLRW.deSitter`, `FLRW.friedmannSolution_deSitter`: the de Sitter model, defined at all
  times, filled with the empty cosmic fluid solves the Friedmann equations.
- `FLRW.not_bddBelow_deSitter_I`: the interval of the de Sitter model is not bounded below.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scale factor and its derivatives
- B. The Friedmann equations
- C. The Hubble and deceleration parameters
- D. The de Sitter model
- E. The de Sitter model is defined at all times

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deSitterScaleFactor
declarations.doc:
The de Sitter scale factor `a(t) = a₀ exp(σ √(Λ/3) c t)`, for `σ = ±1`
(the expanding branch is `σ = 1`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def deSitterScaleFactor (a₀ σ Λ : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) : Time → ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_deSitterScaleFactor
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deSitterScaleFactor (a₀ σ Λ : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    ∂ₜ (deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c) =
      fun t => a₀ * (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ)) * Real.exp (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ) * t.val)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_deriv_deSitterScaleFactor
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_deSitterScaleFactor (a₀ σ Λ : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c)) =
      fun t => a₀ * (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ)) * (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ)) *
        Real.exp (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ) * t.val)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.sq_deSitterRate
declarations.doc: `σ² (√(Λ/3))² c² = Λ c² / 3` for `σ = ±1` and `0 ≤ Λ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sq_deSitterRate {σ Λ : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hΛ : 0 ≤ Λ) (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) :
    (σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ)) ^ 2 = Λ * (c : ℝ) ^ 2 / 3

declarations.doc:
The de Sitter scale factor solves the first-order Friedmann equation with `ρ = 0`,
`k = 0` and `Λ > 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deSitterScaleFactor_firstOrderFriedmann {a₀ σ Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hΛ : 0 < Λ)
    (ha₀ : a₀ ≠ 0) (hσ : σ = 1 ∨ σ = -1) (t : Time) :
    FirstOrderFriedmann (deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c) (fun _ => 0) 0 Λ G c t

declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
lemma deSitterScaleFactor_secondOrderFriedmann {a₀ σ Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hΛ : 0 < Λ)

    SecondOrderFriedmann (deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c) (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) Λ G c t

    hubbleConstant (deSitterScaleFactor a₀ σ Λ c) t = σ * √(Λ / 3) * (c : ℝ)

modules.title: Distances and redshift in FLRW cosmology
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The distances of this file are defined for an FLRW model. They have their meaning at the times
of the interval of the model.

The comoving distance of a source emitting at the time `t` and observed at `t₀` is
`χ = c ∫_t^{t₀} dτ / a(τ)`, so that `∂ₜ χ = - c / a`. The redshift is `1 + z = a(t₀) / a(t)`,
with `∂ₜ z = -(1 + z) H`. Combining the two gives `∂ₜ χ = (c / (a(t₀) H)) ∂ₜ z`. For
`a(t₀) = 1`, this is the change of variables `dχ = c dz / H` behind the distance integrals in the
redshift.

The proper distance `D = a χ` obeys the Hubble-Lemaître law `∂ₜ D = H D`. The recession velocity
equals `c` exactly at the Hubble radius `R_H = c / H`.

The transverse comoving distance `r(χ)` is the function `S` of the spatial geometry of the model.
Its closed forms are written in the curvature parameter `K` of that geometry, with curvature
radius `1 / √|K|`.

The particle and event horizons at `t` integrate `c / a` over the times of the interval of the
model before and after `t`. The particle horizon of the Einstein-de Sitter model
`FLRW.einsteinDeSitter` is computed.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.comovingDistance`, `FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance`: `∂ₜ χ = - c / a`.
- `FLRW.redshift`, `FLRW.deriv_redshift`: `∂ₜ z = -(1 + z) H`.
- `FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance_eq_mul_deriv_redshift`: `∂ₜ χ = (c / (a(t₀) H)) ∂ₜ z`.
- `FLRW.properDistance`, `FLRW.deriv_properDistance`: the Hubble-Lemaître law.
- `FLRW.hubbleRadius`, `FLRW.deriv_properDistance_eq_iff`: the recession velocity at the Hubble
  radius.
- `FLRW.transverseComovingDistance` and its three closed forms.
- `FLRW.particleHorizon`, `FLRW.eventHorizon`, `FLRW.particleHorizon_einsteinDeSitter`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The comoving distance
- B. The redshift and the change of variables
- C. The proper distance and the Hubble radius
- D. The transverse comoving distance
- E. The horizons

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.comovingDistance
declarations.doc:
The line-of-sight comoving distance `χ = c ∫_t^{t₀} dτ / a(τ)` of a source emitting at `t`
and observed at `t₀`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def comovingDistance (c : SpeedOfLight) (t t₀ : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance
declarations.doc: For `t` and `t₀` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ χ = - c / a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comovingDistance {c : SpeedOfLight} {t₀ t : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => U.comovingDistance c s t₀) t = -(c : ℝ) / U.a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.redshift
declarations.doc:
The redshift `z` of a source emitting at `t` and observed at `t₀`, with
`1 + z = a(t₀) / a(t)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def redshift (t₀ t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.one_add_redshift
declarations.statement: lemma one_add_redshift (t₀ t : Time) : 1 + U.redshift t₀ t = U.a t₀ / U.a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_redshift
declarations.doc: For `t` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ z = -(1 + z) H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_redshift {t₀ t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (U.redshift t₀) t = -(1 + U.redshift t₀ t) * hubbleConstant U.a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_scaleFactor_eq_mul_hubbleConstant
declarations.doc: For `t` in the interval of the model, `∂ₜ a = a H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_scaleFactor_eq_mul_hubbleConstant {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ U.a t = U.a t * hubbleConstant U.a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_comovingDistance_eq_mul_deriv_redshift
declarations.doc:
For `t` and `t₀` in the interval of the model with `H(t) ≠ 0`,
`∂ₜ χ = (c / (a(t₀) H)) ∂ₜ z`. For `a(t₀) = 1`, this is the change of variables
`dχ = c dz / H`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comovingDistance_eq_mul_deriv_redshift {c : SpeedOfLight} {t₀ t : Time}
    (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => U.comovingDistance c s t₀) t
      = (c : ℝ) / (U.a t₀ * hubbleConstant U.a t) * ∂ₜ (U.redshift t₀) t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.properDistance
declarations.doc: The proper distance `D = a χ` at fixed comoving distance `χ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def properDistance (χ : ℝ) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_properDistance
declarations.doc: The Hubble-Lemaître law `∂ₜ D = H D`, for `t` in the interval of the model.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_properDistance {χ : ℝ} {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    ∂ₜ (U.properDistance χ) t = hubbleConstant U.a t * U.properDistance χ t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.hubbleRadius
declarations.doc: The Hubble radius `R_H = c / H`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hubbleRadius (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.deriv_properDistance_eq_iff
declarations.doc:
For `t` in the interval of the model with `H(t) ≠ 0`, the recession velocity `∂ₜ D` equals
`c` exactly at the Hubble radius.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_properDistance_eq_iff {χ : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I)
    (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (U.properDistance χ) t = (c : ℝ) ↔ U.properDistance χ t = U.hubbleRadius c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.transverseComovingDistance
declarations.doc: The transverse comoving distance `r(χ) = S(χ)` for the spatial geometry of an FLRW model.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def transverseComovingDistance (χ : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_pos
declarations.doc: For a positive curvature parameter `K`, `r(χ) = (1 / √K) sin (√K χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_pos (hK : 0 < U.geometry.curvature) (χ : ℝ) :
    U.transverseComovingDistance χ
      = 1 / √U.geometry.curvature * Real.sin (√U.geometry.curvature * χ)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_eq_zero
declarations.doc: For a zero curvature parameter, `r(χ) = χ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_eq_zero (hK : U.geometry.curvature = 0) (χ : ℝ) :
    U.transverseComovingDistance χ = χ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_neg
declarations.doc: For a negative curvature parameter `K`, `r(χ) = (1 / √(-K)) sinh (√(-K) χ)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma transverseComovingDistance_of_curvature_neg (hK : U.geometry.curvature < 0) (χ : ℝ) :
    U.transverseComovingDistance χ
      = 1 / √(-U.geometry.curvature) * Real.sinh (√(-U.geometry.curvature) * χ)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.particleHorizon
declarations.doc:
The particle horizon at `t`, the integral of `c / a` over the times of the interval of the
model before `t`. It is a Lebesgue integral, equal to `0` when the integrand is not
integrable.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def particleHorizon (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.eventHorizon
declarations.doc:
The event horizon at `t`, the integral of `c / a` over the times of the interval of the
model after `t`. It is a Lebesgue integral, equal to `0` when the integrand is not

declarations.statement: noncomputable def eventHorizon (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.particleHorizon_einsteinDeSitter
declarations.doc: The particle horizon of the Einstein-de Sitter model at `t > 0` is `3 c t₀^(2/3) t^(1/3)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma particleHorizon_einsteinDeSitter {t₀ : Time} {c : SpeedOfLight} (ht₀ : 0 < t₀.val)

    (einsteinDeSitter t₀ ht₀).particleHorizon c t
      = 3 * (c : ℝ) * t₀.val ^ (2 / 3 : ℝ) * t.val ^ (1 / 3 : ℝ)

modules.title: Energy conditions of the cosmic fluid

## i. Overview

The null, weak, strong and dominant energy conditions of a cosmic fluid `F : CosmicFluid`
(`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`), described by its total energy density `F.ρ` and its pressure

  `CosmicFluid.WeakEnergyCondition.nullEnergyCondition`,
  `CosmicFluid.StrongEnergyCondition.nullEnergyCondition`: the implications between them.

modules.title: Solutions of the Friedmann equations: dynamical criteria
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Qualitative consequences of the Friedmann equations for an FLRW model `U : FLRW` filled with a
cosmic fluid `F : CosmicFluid` that solves them, `U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c`. The proposition
`FLRW.FriedmannSolution` itself is defined in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`, together with the
tangent-line bound for a decelerating FLRW model, which does not use the Friedmann equations; the
continuity equation (`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.MatterContent`) and the density parameters, which
are used here, are stated about it. The energy conditions of the cosmic fluid are in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.EnergyConditions`. On the interval `U.I` of the model: a solution with
cosmological constant `Λ` is a solution without it for the fluid with `Λ` folded in; the
expansion accelerates if and only if the fluid, with the cosmological constant folded in as a
`w = -1` component, violates the strong energy condition; the deceleration parameter is
`q = ½ Σ_x Ω_x (1 + 3 w_x)` for a finite family of barotropic fluids, and
`q = ½ (Ω_m + 2 Ω_r - 2 Ω_Λ)` for ΛCDM; with a spatial geometry of non-positive curvature,
positive density and `0 ≤ Λ`, the derivative `∂ₜ a` of the scale factor does not vanish, so that
a model expanding at one time of `U.I` expands at all times of `U.I`. Finally, with `0 ≤ ρ`,
`0 ≤ p` and `Λ = 0` the scale factor decelerates on `U.I`, so that a model expanding at
`t₀ ∈ U.I` cannot be defined at any time earlier than `t₀ - 1 / H(t₀)`: its interval of time is
bounded below, the Big Bang being at most `1 / H(t₀)` in the past. The de Sitter model of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.DeSitter`, with `0 < Λ`, is defined at all times.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.friedmannSolution_iff_addCosmologicalConstant`: a solution with `Λ` is a solution
  without `Λ` for the fluid `F.addCosmologicalConstant Λ G c`.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff`: `0 < ∂ₜ ∂ₜ a ↔ ρ + 3 p / c² < 0`
  (`Λ = 0`); `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff_lambda`: the same for the
  total fluid with `Λ` folded in.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.decelerationParameter_eq_sum`: `q = ½ Σ_i Ω_i (1 + 3 w_i)`;
  `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.decelerationParameter_lambdaCDM`: `q = ½ (Ω_m + 2 Ω_r - 2 Ω_Λ)`.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_scaleFactor_ne_zero`,
  `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_scaleFactor_pos`: eternal expansion for a non-positive curvature.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_nonpos`,
  `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.lt_of_mem_I`, `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.bddBelow_I`: the Big-Bang bound.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The cosmological constant folded into the cosmic fluid
- B. Accelerated expansion and the strong energy condition
- C. The deceleration parameter in terms of the density parameters
- D. Eternal expansion
- E. The Big-Bang bound for a solution of the Friedmann equations

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.friedmannSolution_iff_addCosmologicalConstant
declarations.doc:
An FLRW model filled with the cosmic fluid `F` solves the Friedmann equations with the
cosmological constant `Λ` if and only if it solves them without cosmological constant for the
fluid `F` with `Λ` folded in.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff
declarations.doc:
On the interval of a solution without cosmological constant, the second derivative
`∂ₜ ∂ₜ a` of the scale factor is positive (the expansion accelerates) if and only if
`ρ + 3 p / c² < 0`, that is, if and only if the strong energy condition of the cosmic fluid
fails through its second inequality.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) (hG : 0 < G) {t : Time}
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) : 0 < ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) t ↔ F.ρ t + 3 * F.p t / (c : ℝ) ^ 2 < 0

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff_lambda
declarations.doc:
With cosmological constant `Λ`, on the interval of a solution, `∂ₜ ∂ₜ a` is positive if and
only if the total fluid, `Λ` folded in as the `w = -1` component, violates
`0 ≤ ρ + 3 p / c²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_pos_iff_lambda (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c) (hG : 0 < G)
    {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    0 < ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) t ↔ (F.ρ t + cosmologicalConstantDensity Λ G c)
      + 3 * (F.p t + cosmologicalConstantPressure Λ G c) / (c : ℝ) ^ 2 < 0

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.decelerationParameter_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
For a solution of the Friedmann equations without cosmological constant whose cosmic fluid is
a sum of barotropic components of pressure `w_i ρ_i c²`, the deceleration parameter is
`q = ½ Σ_i Ω_i (1 + 3 w_i)` at the times of the interval of the model at which `H ≠ 0`, for
`G ≠ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma decelerationParameter_eq_sum {n : ℕ} {Fi : Fin n → CosmicFluid} {w : Fin n → ℝ}
    (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) (hG : G ≠ 0) (hρ : ∀ s, F.ρ s = ∑ i, (Fi i).ρ s)
    (hp : ∀ s, F.p s = ∑ i, (Fi i).p s) (hw : ∀ i, (Fi i).p = barotropicPressure (w i) (Fi i).ρ c)
    {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hH : hubbleConstant U.a t ≠ 0) :
    decelerationParameter U.a t
      = 1 / 2 * ∑ i, U.densityParameter (Fi i) G t * (1 + 3 * w i)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.decelerationParameter_lambdaCDM
declarations.doc:
For a solution of the Friedmann equations whose cosmic fluid is the sum of matter (zero
pressure) and radiation (pressure `ρ_r c² / 3`), the deceleration parameter is
`q = ½ (Ω_m + 2 Ω_r - 2 Ω_Λ)` at the times of the interval of the model (the ΛCDM case).
declarations.statement:
lemma decelerationParameter_lambdaCDM {Fm Fr : CosmicFluid} (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c)
    (hρ : ∀ s, F.ρ s = Fm.ρ s + Fr.ρ s) (hp : ∀ s, F.p s = Fm.p s + Fr.p s)
    (hm : Fm.p = barotropicPressure 0 Fm.ρ c) (hr : Fr.p = barotropicPressure (1 / 3) Fr.ρ c)
    {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    decelerationParameter U.a t = 1 / 2 * (U.densityParameter Fm G t
      + 2 * U.densityParameter Fr G t - 2 * U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_scaleFactor_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
For a spatial geometry of non-positive curvature parameter, `0 ≤ Λ` and a positive density
at a time `t` of the interval, the first-order Friedmann equation forces `0 < H²` at `t`:
the derivative `∂ₜ a` of the scale factor does not vanish at `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_scaleFactor_ne_zero (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c)
    (hk : U.geometry.curvature ≤ 0) (hΛ : 0 ≤ Λ) (hG : 0 < G) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I)
    (hρ : 0 < F.ρ t) : ∂ₜ U.a t ≠ 0

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_scaleFactor_pos
declarations.doc:
If moreover the density is positive on the interval and the model expands at one time `t₀`
of `U.I`, it expands at all times of `U.I`: with a non-positive curvature parameter, `0 ≤ Λ`
and a positive density, an expanding model expands forever.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_scaleFactor_pos (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c) (hk : U.geometry.curvature ≤ 0)
    (hΛ : 0 ≤ Λ) (hG : 0 < G) (hρ : ∀ s ∈ U.I, 0 < F.ρ s) {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I)
    (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) {t : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_nonpos
declarations.doc:
With `0 ≤ ρ`, `0 ≤ p` and `Λ = 0` at a time `t` of the interval, the second-order Friedmann
equation gives `∂ₜ ∂ₜ a ≤ 0` at `t`: the expansion decelerates.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_scaleFactor_nonpos (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) (hG : 0 < G) {t : Time}
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) (hρ : 0 ≤ F.ρ t) (hp : 0 ≤ F.p t) : ∂ₜ (∂ₜ U.a) t ≤ 0

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.lt_of_mem_I
declarations.doc:
The Big-Bang bound for a solution of the Friedmann equations with `0 ≤ ρ`, `0 ≤ p` and
`Λ = 0` on its interval: if the model expands at `t₀ ∈ U.I`, every time of `U.I` is later than
`t₀ - 1 / H(t₀)`, the Big Bang being at most `1 / H(t₀)` in the past.
declarations.statement:
lemma lt_of_mem_I (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) (hG : 0 < G) (hρ : ∀ s ∈ U.I, 0 ≤ F.ρ s)
    (hp : ∀ s ∈ U.I, 0 ≤ F.p s) {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) {t : Time}
    (ht : t ∈ U.I) :
    t₀.val - 1 / hubbleConstant U.a t₀ < t.val

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.bddBelow_I
declarations.doc: Under the same assumptions, the interval of the model is bounded below.
declarations.statement:
lemma bddBelow_I (h : U.FriedmannSolution F 0 G c) (hG : 0 < G) (hρ : ∀ s ∈ U.I, 0 ≤ F.ρ s)
    (hp : ∀ s ∈ U.I, 0 ≤ F.p s) {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I) (h0 : 0 < ∂ₜ U.a t₀) :
    BddBelow U.I

modules.title: Matter content of FLRW cosmology
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This file describes the matter content of a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe
through the continuity equation `∂ₜ ρ + 3 H (ρ + p / c²) = 0` of the cosmic fluid and its
relation to the two Friedmann equations of `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`: the continuity
equation follows from the first-order equation (holding at all times near the instant
considered) and the second-order equation, and conversely the second-order equation follows
from the first-order equation and the continuity equation whenever `∂ₜ a ≠ 0`. The three
equations are therefore not independent, but not symmetrically so: where `∂ₜ a = 0` the
first-order and the continuity equations leave `p` unconstrained, while the second-order
equation still fixes `ρ + 3 p / c²` (the Einstein static universe of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Solutions`). The two Friedmann equations are the primitive pair, and
the continuity equation is derived from them; accordingly, the proposition
`FLRW.FriedmannSolution` consists of the two Friedmann equations, and the continuity equation is
the lemma `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.continuityEquation`. For a barotropic equation of state
`p = w ρ c²` with
constant `w`, the continuity equation gives the density scaling law `ρ ∝ a^(-3(1+w))`,
specialised to dust, radiation and vacuum energy; and the cosmological constant is equivalent
to a `w = -1` fluid of density `ρ_Λ = Λ c² / (8 π G)`. The perfect-fluid stress-energy
tensor is still a TODO item.

Time derivatives of curves `Time → ℝ` are computed through the bridge
`Time.hasDerivAt_mk_of_differentiableAt` to Mathlib's `HasDerivAt` on `ℝ`.

## ii. Key results

- `ContinuityEquation`: the continuity equation at an instant `t`.
- `deriv_firstOrderFriedmann`: the time derivative of the first-order Friedmann equation,
  `2 H (a''/a - H²) = (8 π G / 3) ρ' + 2 k c² H / a²`.
- `continuityEquation_of_friedmann`: the continuity equation follows from the two Friedmann
  equations.
- `secondOrderFriedmann_of_continuityEquation`: the second-order Friedmann equation follows
  from the first-order equation and the continuity equation when `∂ₜ a ≠ 0`.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.continuityEquation`: the continuity equation holds on the interval of
  an FLRW model whose cosmic fluid solves the Friedmann equations.
- `barotropicPressure`: `p = w ρ c²`; `density_scaling`: under the barotropic continuity
  equation at all times, `ρ t = ρ t₀ (a t / a t₀)^(-3(1+w))`; `continuityEquation_of_scaling`:
  the converse; `density_scaling_dust`, `density_scaling_radiation`,
  `density_scaling_vacuum`: `ρ ∝ a⁻³`, `ρ ∝ a⁻⁴`, `ρ` constant.
- `firstOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid`, `secondOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid`: the Friedmann
  equations with `Λ` are the Friedmann equations without `Λ` for the fluid `ρ + ρ_Λ`, `p + p_Λ`,
  where `ρ_Λ = Λ c² / (8 π G)` and `p_Λ = - ρ_Λ c²` (`cosmologicalConstantDensity` and
  `cosmologicalConstantPressure`, defined in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`);
  `cosmologicalConstantPressure_eq_barotropic`: `p_Λ` is the `w = -1` barotropic pressure.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The continuity equation
  - A.1. The definition
  - A.2. The derivative of the first-order Friedmann equation
  - A.3. Continuity from the Friedmann equations
  - A.4. The second-order Friedmann equation from continuity
  - A.5. The continuity equation of a solution of the Friedmann equations
- B. The barotropic equation of state and the density scaling law
  - B.1. The equation of state
  - B.2. The density scaling law
  - B.3. Dust, radiation and vacuum energy
- C. The cosmological constant as a fluid
- D. Remaining TODO items

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.ContinuityEquation
declarations.doc:
The continuity equation of the cosmic fluid at the instant `t`:
`∂ₜ ρ + 3 H (ρ + p / c²) = 0`, with `H = hubbleConstant a`.
declarations.statement: def ContinuityEquation (a ρ p : Time → ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) : Prop

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_firstOrderFriedmann
declarations.doc:
Differentiating the first-order Friedmann equation, assumed at all times near `t`, at `t`:
`2 H (a''/a - H²) = (8 π G / 3) ρ' + 2 k c² H / a²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_firstOrderFriedmann {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {k Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} {t : Time}
    (ha : a t ≠ 0) (hd1 : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t) (hd2 : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (hdρ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ρ t) (hF1 : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 t, FirstOrderFriedmann a ρ k Λ G c s) :
    2 * (∂ₜ a t / a t) * (∂ₜ (∂ₜ a) t / a t - (∂ₜ a t / a t) ^ 2)
      = 8 * π * G / 3 * ∂ₜ ρ t + 2 * k * (c : ℝ) ^ 2 * (∂ₜ a t / a t) / (a t) ^ 2

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.continuityEquation_of_friedmann
declarations.doc:
The continuity equation follows from the first-order Friedmann equation, assumed at all
times near `t`, and the second-order Friedmann equation at `t`; `a` must be twice
differentiable and `ρ` differentiable at `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuityEquation_of_friedmann {a ρ p : Time → ℝ} {k Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight}
    {t : Time} (hG : G ≠ 0) (ha : a t ≠ 0) (hd1 : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t)
    (hd2 : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t)
    (hdρ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ρ t) (hF1 : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 t, FirstOrderFriedmann a ρ k Λ G c s)
    (hF2 : SecondOrderFriedmann a ρ p Λ G c t) :
    ContinuityEquation a ρ p c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.secondOrderFriedmann_of_continuityEquation
declarations.doc:
The second-order Friedmann equation at `t` follows from the first-order Friedmann
equation, assumed at all times near `t`, and the continuity equation at `t`, provided
`∂ₜ a t ≠ 0`. Together with `continuityEquation_of_friedmann`, the three equations are not
independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma secondOrderFriedmann_of_continuityEquation {a ρ p : Time → ℝ} {k Λ G : ℝ}
    {c : SpeedOfLight} {t : Time} (ha : a t ≠ 0) (ha' : ∂ₜ a t ≠ 0) (hd1 : DifferentiableAt ℝ a t)
    (hd2 : DifferentiableAt ℝ (∂ₜ a) t) (hdρ : DifferentiableAt ℝ ρ t)
    (hF1 : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝 t, FirstOrderFriedmann a ρ k Λ G c s)
    (hC : ContinuityEquation a ρ p c t) :
    SecondOrderFriedmann a ρ p Λ G c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.continuityEquation
declarations.doc:
If the FLRW model `U` filled with the cosmic fluid `F` solves the Friedmann equations, the
continuity equation holds at every time of the interval `U.I` at which the energy density is
differentiable: it is obtained from the two Friedmann equations through
`continuityEquation_of_friedmann`.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.barotropicPressure
declarations.doc: The barotropic pressure `p = w ρ c²` with constant equation-of-state parameter `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def barotropicPressure (w : ℝ) (ρ : Time → ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) : Time → ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_of_continuityEquation_barotropic
declarations.doc: Under the barotropic continuity equation, `∂ₜ ρ = -3 (1 + w) H ρ`.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.density_scaling
declarations.doc:
The density scaling law: under the barotropic continuity equation at all times, with `a`
and `ρ` differentiable and `a > 0`, `ρ t = ρ t₀ (a t / a t₀)^(-3(1+w))`. The proof shows that
`ρ a^(3(1+w))` has zero derivative along the time chart.
declarations.statement:
lemma density_scaling {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {w : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hd1 : Differentiable ℝ a)
    (hdρ : Differentiable ℝ ρ) (hapos : ∀ s, 0 < a s)
    (hC : ∀ s, ContinuityEquation a ρ (barotropicPressure w ρ c) c s) (t t₀ : Time) :
    ρ t = ρ t₀ * (a t / a t₀) ^ (-(3 * (1 + w)))

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.continuityEquation_of_scaling
declarations.doc:
Conversely, `ρ = ρ₀ (a / a₀)^(-3(1+w))` satisfies the barotropic continuity equation at
all times, for `a` differentiable and positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuityEquation_of_scaling {a : Time → ℝ} {w : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} {ρ₀ a₀ : ℝ}
    (ha₀ : a₀ ≠ 0) (hd1 : Differentiable ℝ a) (hapos : ∀ s, 0 < a s) (t : Time) :
    ContinuityEquation a (fun s => ρ₀ * (a s / a₀) ^ (-(3 * (1 + w))))
      (barotropicPressure w (fun s => ρ₀ * (a s / a₀) ^ (-(3 * (1 + w)))) c) c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.density_scaling_dust
declarations.doc: Dust, `w = 0`: `ρ ∝ a⁻³`.
declarations.statement:
lemma density_scaling_dust {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hd1 : Differentiable ℝ a)
    (hdρ : Differentiable ℝ ρ) (hapos : ∀ s, 0 < a s)
    (hC : ∀ s, ContinuityEquation a ρ (barotropicPressure 0 ρ c) c s) (t t₀ : Time) :
    ρ t = ρ t₀ * (a t₀ / a t) ^ 3

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.density_scaling_radiation
declarations.doc: Radiation, `w = 1/3`: `ρ ∝ a⁻⁴`.
declarations.statement:
lemma density_scaling_radiation {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hd1 : Differentiable ℝ a)
    (hdρ : Differentiable ℝ ρ) (hapos : ∀ s, 0 < a s)
    (hC : ∀ s, ContinuityEquation a ρ (barotropicPressure (1 / 3) ρ c) c s) (t t₀ : Time) :
    ρ t = ρ t₀ * (a t₀ / a t) ^ 4

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.density_scaling_vacuum
declarations.doc: Vacuum energy, `w = -1`: `ρ` is constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma density_scaling_vacuum {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hd1 : Differentiable ℝ a)
    (hdρ : Differentiable ℝ ρ) (hapos : ∀ s, 0 < a s)
    (hC : ∀ s, ContinuityEquation a ρ (barotropicPressure (-1) ρ c) c s) (t t₀ : Time) :
    ρ t = ρ t₀

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.firstOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid
declarations.doc:
The first-order Friedmann equation with `Λ` is the first-order Friedmann equation without
`Λ` for the density `ρ + ρ_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma firstOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid {a ρ : Time → ℝ} {k Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight}
    {t : Time} (hG : G ≠ 0) :
    FirstOrderFriedmann a ρ k Λ G c t ↔
      FirstOrderFriedmann a (fun s => ρ s + cosmologicalConstantDensity Λ G c) k 0 G c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.secondOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid
declarations.doc:
The second-order Friedmann equation with `Λ` is the second-order Friedmann equation
without `Λ` for the density `ρ + ρ_Λ` and the pressure `p + p_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma secondOrderFriedmann_iff_lambdaFluid {a ρ p : Time → ℝ} {Λ G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight}
    {t : Time} (hG : G ≠ 0) :
    SecondOrderFriedmann a ρ p Λ G c t ↔
      SecondOrderFriedmann a (fun s => ρ s + cosmologicalConstantDensity Λ G c)
        (fun s => p s + cosmologicalConstantPressure Λ G c) 0 G c t

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.cosmologicalConstantPressure_eq_barotropic
declarations.doc: `p_Λ` is the barotropic pressure of `ρ_Λ` with `w = -1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cosmologicalConstantPressure_eq_barotropic (Λ G : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) (t : Time) :
    cosmologicalConstantPressure Λ G c
      = barotropicPressure (-1) (fun _ => cosmologicalConstantDensity Λ G c) c t

modules.title: The reduced Hubble function of the standard cosmological model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The reduced Hubble function of the standard cosmological model is
`E(x) = √(Ω_Λ + Ω_m x⁻³ + Ω_r x⁻⁴ + Ω_K x⁻²)`, with the density parameters of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.DensityParameters` taken at a reference time `t₀`. For an FLRW model
filled with matter (`ρ ∝ a⁻³`) and radiation (`ρ ∝ a⁻⁴`) that solves the Friedmann equations, the
Hubble parameter is `H = H₀ E(a / a₀)` with `H₀ = H(t₀) > 0` and `H ≥ 0`. The scaling laws of the
densities between `t₀` and `t` are hypotheses, not derived here.

The equality scale factors are the values of `x = a / a₀` at which two terms of `E²` are equal:
radiation and matter at `a_eq = Ω_r / Ω_m`, matter and cosmological constant at
`a_Λ = (Ω_m / Ω_Λ)^(1/3)`.

## ii. Key results

- `reducedHubble`: the reduced Hubble function of the standard model.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.sq_hubbleConstant_eq_mul_densityParameters`: the normalised Friedmann
  equation `H² = H₀² (Ω_Λ + Ω_m x⁻³ + Ω_r x⁻⁴ + Ω_K x⁻²)` with `x = a / a₀`.
- `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.sq_hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble`,
  `FLRW.FriedmannSolution.hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble`: `H² = H₀² E(a / a₀)²` and
  `H = H₀ E(a / a₀)`.
- `equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter`, `equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda` and the equalities
  they realise.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The reduced Hubble function
- B. The equality scale factors
- C. The Hubble parameter of a solution of the Friedmann equations

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.reducedHubble
declarations.doc:
The reduced Hubble function `E(x) = √(Ω_Λ + Ω_m x⁻³ + Ω_r x⁻⁴ + Ω_K x⁻²)` of the standard
cosmological model: the Hubble parameter in units of its value `H₀` at the reference time,
as a function of the scale factor `x = a / a₀` in units of its reference value. The four
terms are the shares of the cosmological constant, matter, radiation and curvature at the
reference time, each diluted by its own power of `x`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def reducedHubble (ΩΛ Ωm Ωr ΩK x : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter
declarations.doc:
The radiation-matter equality scale factor `a_eq = Ω_r / Ω_m`: the value of `x = a / a₀`
at which the matter and radiation terms of `E²` are equal; radiation dominates before it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter (Ωr Ωm : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda
declarations.doc:
The matter-Λ equality scale factor `a_Λ = (Ω_m / Ω_Λ)^(1/3)`: the value of `x = a / a₀`
at which the matter term of `E²` equals `Ω_Λ`; the cosmological constant dominates after
it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda (Ωm ΩΛ : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter_spec
declarations.doc: At `a_eq`, the matter and radiation terms of `E²` are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter_spec {Ωr Ωm : ℝ} (hr : 0 < Ωr) (hm : 0 < Ωm) :
    Ωm * equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter Ωr Ωm ^ (-3 : ℝ)
      = Ωr * equalityScaleFactorRadiationMatter Ωr Ωm ^ (-4 : ℝ)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda_spec
declarations.doc: At `a_Λ`, the matter term of `E²` equals `Ω_Λ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda_spec {Ωm ΩΛ : ℝ} (hm : 0 < Ωm) (hL : 0 < ΩΛ) :
    Ωm * equalityScaleFactorMatterLambda Ωm ΩΛ ^ (-3 : ℝ) = ΩΛ

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.sq_hubbleConstant_eq_mul_densityParameters
declarations.doc:
For a solution of the Friedmann equations whose density is that of matter plus that of
radiation, take two times `t` and `t₀` of the interval of the model with `H(t₀) ≠ 0` at which
`ρ_m(t) = ρ_m(t₀) (a(t₀) / a(t))³` and `ρ_r(t) = ρ_r(t₀) (a(t₀) / a(t))⁴`. Then
`H² = H₀² (Ω_Λ + Ω_m x⁻³ + Ω_r x⁻⁴ + Ω_K x⁻²)` with `x = a(t) / a(t₀)` and the density
parameters taken at `t₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sq_hubbleConstant_eq_mul_densityParameters (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c)
    (hρ : ∀ s, F.ρ s = Fm.ρ s + Fr.ρ s) {t t₀ : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I)
    (hH₀ : hubbleConstant U.a t₀ ≠ 0)
    (hm : Fm.ρ t = Fm.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 3) (hr : Fr.ρ t = Fr.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 4) :
    hubbleConstant U.a t ^ 2 = hubbleConstant U.a t₀ ^ 2
      * (U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t₀ + U.densityParameter Fm G t₀ * (U.a t / U.a t₀) ^ (-3 : ℝ)
        + U.densityParameter Fr G t₀ * (U.a t / U.a t₀) ^ (-4 : ℝ)
        + U.curvatureDensityParameter c t₀ * (U.a t / U.a t₀) ^ (-2 : ℝ))

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.sq_hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble
declarations.doc:
`H² = H₀² E(a / a₀)²`, under the hypotheses of
`sq_hubbleConstant_eq_mul_densityParameters`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sq_hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c)
    (hρ : ∀ s, F.ρ s = Fm.ρ s + Fr.ρ s) {t t₀ : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I)
    (hH₀ : hubbleConstant U.a t₀ ≠ 0)
    (hm : Fm.ρ t = Fm.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 3) (hr : Fr.ρ t = Fr.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 4) :
    hubbleConstant U.a t ^ 2 = hubbleConstant U.a t₀ ^ 2
      * reducedHubble (U.lambdaDensityParameter Λ c t₀) (U.densityParameter Fm G t₀)
        (U.densityParameter Fr G t₀) (U.curvatureDensityParameter c t₀) (U.a t / U.a t₀) ^ 2

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannSolution.hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble
declarations.doc:
`H = H₀ E(a / a₀)` for `0 < H₀` and `0 ≤ H`, under the hypotheses of
`sq_hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hubbleConstant_eq_reducedHubble (h : U.FriedmannSolution F Λ G c)
    (hρ : ∀ s, F.ρ s = Fm.ρ s + Fr.ρ s) {t t₀ : Time} (ht : t ∈ U.I) (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ U.I)
    (hH₀ : 0 < hubbleConstant U.a t₀) (hH : 0 ≤ hubbleConstant U.a t)
    (hm : Fm.ρ t = Fm.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 3) (hr : Fr.ρ t = Fr.ρ t₀ * (U.a t₀ / U.a t) ^ 4) :

        (U.densityParameter Fr G t₀) (U.curvatureDensityParameter c t₀) (U.a t / U.a t₀)

modules.title: Exact solutions of the Friedmann equations
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This file collects the standard closed-form solutions of the Friedmann equations
(`FirstOrderFriedmann` and `SecondOrderFriedmann` of `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Basic`) and
proves that they solve them: the spatially flat power-law solutions (radiation-dominated
and Einstein-de Sitter), the Milne model, and the equilibrium relations of the Einstein static
universe. The de Sitter solution is in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.DeSitter`. The vanishing of the
curvature of the Milne model and the instability of the Einstein static universe are still TODO
items: neither the curvature of the FLRW metric nor a perturbation theory of the Friedmann
equations is available yet.

The flat power-law solutions are also given as FLRW models: `FLRW.powerLaw` in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.PowerLaw`, `FLRW.radiationDominated` in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.RadiationDominated` and `FLRW.einsteinDeSitter` in
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.EinsteinDeSitter`.

Each solution is a scale factor `a : Time → ℝ` given by an explicit function of the time
coordinate `t.val`. Its time derivative `∂ₜ a` is computed through the bridge
`deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt` from Mathlib's `HasDerivAt` on `ℝ`.

## ii. Key results

- `hubbleConstant_powerLaw`, `decelerationParameter_powerLaw`, `powerLaw_firstOrderFriedmann`,
  `powerLaw_secondOrderFriedmann`: the flat power-law solutions `a = (t / t₀) ^ n`, stated
  inline, have Hubble parameter `n / t` and deceleration parameter `(1 - n) / n`, and solve the
  flat (`k = 0`, `Λ = 0`) Friedmann equations with the density `ρ = 3 n² / (8 π G t²)` and the
  pressure `p = w ρ c²`, `1 + 3 w = 2 (1 - n) / n`, for `t > 0`.
- `radiationScaleFactor_firstOrderFriedmann`, `radiationScaleFactor_secondOrderFriedmann`:
  `a = (t / t₀) ^ (1/2)` solves the flat Friedmann equations with the density
  `ρ = 3 / (32 π G t²)` and the radiation pressure `p = ρ c² / 3`; `q = 1` and
  `H(t₀) = 1 / (2 t₀)`.
- `einsteinDeSitterScaleFactor_firstOrderFriedmann`,
  `einsteinDeSitterScaleFactor_secondOrderFriedmann`: `a = (t / t₀) ^ (2/3)` solves the flat
  Friedmann equations with the dust density `ρ = 1 / (6 π G t²)` and `p = 0`; `q = 1 / 2` and
  `H(t₀) = 2 / (3 t₀)`.

- `milneScaleFactor_firstOrderFriedmann`, `milneScaleFactor_secondOrderFriedmann`: the Milne
  scale factor `a = c t` solves the empty (`ρ = 0`, `p = 0`, `Λ = 0`) Friedmann equations with
  `k = -1`; `q = 0`. `FLRW.milne`, `FLRW.friedmannSolution_milne`: the Milne model on the
  interval `t > 0`, with the saddle geometry of curvature parameter `-1`, filled with the empty
  cosmic fluid solves the Friedmann equations.
- `einsteinStatic_density`, `einsteinStatic_curvature`: if `∂ₜ a = ∂ₜ ∂ₜ a = 0` at `t` and the
  Friedmann equations hold there with `p = 0`, then `ρ = Λ c² / (4 π G)` and
  `k c² / a² = 4 π G ρ`, so that `k > 0` when `ρ > 0` (`einsteinStatic_curvature_pos`).

In the power-law solutions `t₀ : Time` is the normalisation epoch (`a(t₀) = 1`) and the Big
Bang is at the origin `t.val = 0` of the time chart.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The spatially flat power-law solutions
  - A.1. Derivatives of the power-law scale factor
  - A.2. The Hubble and deceleration parameters
  - A.3. The radiation-dominated solution
  - A.4. The Einstein-de Sitter solution
- B. The Milne solution
- C. The Einstein static universe
- D. Remaining TODO items

sections.text:
## A. The spatially flat power-law solutions

The radiation-dominated and Einstein-de Sitter solutions are both of the form
`a(t) = (t / t₀) ^ n`; the Hubble parameter is `n / t` and the deceleration parameter
`(1 - n) / n`. Their densities are imposed by the first-order Friedmann equation with `k = 0`
and `Λ = 0`: `ρ = 3 H² / (8 π G) = 3 n² / (8 π G t²)`. The general power-law solution is
stated inline, only the two named solutions get a definition.

Throughout, `t₀` is the normalisation epoch, `a(t₀) = 1`, the Big Bang sits at the origin
`t.val = 0` of the time chart (`Time` has no distinguished origin by itself), and the values
for `t.val ≤ 0` are junk (`Real.rpow` on a non-positive base); every statement therefore
assumes `0 < t.val`.
### A.1. Derivatives of the power-law scale factor
### A.2. The Hubble and deceleration parameters
### A.3. The radiation-dominated solution
### A.4. The Einstein-de Sitter solution

## B. The Milne solution

The Milne universe is the empty (`ρ = 0`, `p = 0`, `Λ = 0`) solution with `k = -1` and
`a(t) = c t` for `t > 0`. That it is Minkowski space in expanding coordinates (vanishing
curvature) is not stated here: the FLRW metric is not yet an object of Physlib.

## C. The Einstein static universe

At an instant where `∂ₜ a = ∂ₜ ∂ₜ a = 0`, the two Friedmann equations with dust (`p = 0`)
force the density `ρ = Λ c² / (4 π G)` (twice the density `Λ c² / (8 π G)` that the
cosmological constant carries as a `w = -1` fluid, a matter-content statement that belongs to
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.MatterContent`) and `k c² / a² = 4 π G ρ`, hence a positive curvature
parameter when `ρ > 0`. That this equilibrium is unstable is not stated here.
## D. Remaining TODO items

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_powerLaw
declarations.doc: `∂ₜ (t / t₀) ^ n = n / t₀ (t / t₀) ^ (n - 1)` away from `t.val = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_powerLaw {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀.val ≠ 0) (n : ℝ) {t : Time} (ht : t.val ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s : Time => (s.val / t₀.val) ^ n) t = n / t₀.val * (t.val / t₀.val) ^ (n - 1)

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.deriv_deriv_powerLaw
declarations.doc:
`∂ₜ ∂ₜ (t / t₀) ^ n = n (n - 1) / t₀² (t / t₀) ^ (n - 2)` for `0 < t.val`. The first
derivative is only known away from `t.val = 0`, which is enough since `0 < t.val` is an open
condition.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_powerLaw {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : t₀.val ≠ 0) (n : ℝ) {t : Time}
    (ht : 0 < t.val) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun s : Time => (s.val / t₀.val) ^ n)) t =
      n / t₀.val * ((n - 1) / t₀.val * (t.val / t₀.val) ^ (n - 1 - 1))

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.hubbleConstant_powerLaw
declarations.doc: The Hubble parameter of the power-law solution is `n / t` for `0 < t.val`.

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.FriedmannEquation.decelerationParameter_powerLaw

The flat power-law solution solves the first-order Friedmann equation with `k = 0`,
`Λ = 0` and the density `ρ = 3 n² / (8 π G t²)` that it imposes, for `0 < t.val`.

lemma powerLaw_firstOrderFriedmann {t₀ : Time} {G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (ht₀ : 0 < t₀.val)

    FirstOrderFriedmann (fun s : Time => (s.val / t₀.val) ^ n)

declarations.doc: In the Einstein static universe `k c² / a² = 4 π G ρ`.

    k * (c : ℝ) ^ 2 / (a t) ^ 2 = 4 * π * G * ρ t

    (hF2 : SecondOrderFriedmann a ρ (fun _ => 0) Λ G c t) :
    0 < k

modules.title: The Einstein-de Sitter model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Einstein-de Sitter solution `einsteinDeSitterScaleFactor t₀`, `a(t) = (t / t₀) ^ (2/3)`, of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Solutions` as an FLRW model: the flat power-law model of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.PowerLaw` with `n = 2/3`, on the interval `t > 0`. Filled
with its cosmic fluid `CosmicFluid.powerLaw (2/3) 0 G c`, dust of density
`3 n² / (8 π G t²) = 1 / (6 π G t²)` with `n = 2/3` and zero pressure, it solves the Friedmann
equations without cosmological constant.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.einsteinDeSitter`: the Einstein-de Sitter model.
- `FLRW.einsteinDeSitter_a`: its scale factor is `einsteinDeSitterScaleFactor t₀`.
- `FLRW.friedmannSolution_einsteinDeSitter`: filled with dust, it solves the Friedmann
  equations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Einstein-de Sitter model

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The flat power-law models
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The spatially flat power-law solutions `a(t) = (t / t₀) ^ n` of `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Solutions`
as FLRW models. The model `FLRW.powerLaw t₀ ht₀ n` lives on the interval `t > 0`, after the
origin `t.val = 0` of the time chart (for `n > 0`, the Big Bang, where the scale factor vanishes),
for a normalisation epoch `t₀ > 0`, and has flat spatial slices. Filled with the cosmic fluid
`CosmicFluid.powerLaw n w G c`, of density `3 n² / (8 π G t²)` and pressure `w ρ c²`, it solves
the Friedmann equations without cosmological constant when `n ≠ 0` and
`1 + 3 w = 2 (1 - n) / n`. The radiation-dominated and Einstein-de Sitter models, the
cases `n = 1/2` and `n = 2/3`, are in `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.RadiationDominated`
and `Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.EinsteinDeSitter`.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.powerLaw`: the flat power-law model on the interval `t > 0`.
- `CosmicFluid.powerLaw`: the cosmic fluid of the flat power-law solution.
- `FLRW.friedmannSolution_powerLaw`: the model filled with this fluid solves the Friedmann
  equations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The power-law model
- B. The cosmic fluid and the Friedmann equations

declarations.doc:
The spatially flat power-law model `a(t) = (t / t₀) ^ n` on the interval `t > 0`, after the
origin `t.val = 0` of the time chart (for `n > 0`, the Big Bang), for a normalisation epoch

declarations.name: Cosmology.CosmicFluid.powerLaw
declarations.doc:
The cosmic fluid of the flat power-law solution: the density `ρ = 3 n² / (8 π G t²)` imposed by
the first-order Friedmann equation, and the pressure `p = w ρ c²`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def CosmicFluid.powerLaw (n w G : ℝ) (c : SpeedOfLight) : CosmicFluid

declarations.name: Cosmology.FLRW.friedmannSolution_powerLaw
declarations.doc:
The flat power-law model with `n ≠ 0`, filled with the fluid `CosmicFluid.powerLaw n w G c`
where `1 + 3 w = 2 (1 - n) / n`, solves the Friedmann equations without cosmological constant on
its interval `t > 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FLRW.friedmannSolution_powerLaw {t₀ : Time} (ht₀ : 0 < t₀.val)
    {n w G : ℝ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (hG : 0 < G) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hw : 1 + 3 * w = 2 * (1 - n) / n) :
    (FLRW.powerLaw t₀ ht₀ n).FriedmannSolution (CosmicFluid.powerLaw n w G c) 0 G c

modules.title: The radiation-dominated model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The radiation-dominated solution `radiationScaleFactor t₀`, `a(t) = (t / t₀) ^ (1/2)`, of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.Solutions` as an FLRW model: the flat power-law model of
`Physlib.Cosmology.FLRW.SpecificCases.PowerLaw` with `n = 1/2`, on the interval `t > 0`. Filled
with its cosmic fluid `CosmicFluid.powerLaw (1/2) (1/3) G c`, radiation of density
`3 n² / (8 π G t²) = 3 / (32 π G t²)` with `n = 1/2` and pressure `ρ c² / 3`, it solves the
Friedmann equations without cosmological constant.

## ii. Key results

- `FLRW.radiationDominated`: the radiation-dominated model.
- `FLRW.radiationDominated_a`: its scale factor is `radiationScaleFactor t₀`.
- `FLRW.friedmannSolution_radiationDominated`: filled with radiation, it solves the Friedmann
  equations.
